title: The Close Call
logline: In a village cricket match, an umpire has a fraction of a second to decide a dismissal that will end someone's innings, and the whole ground waits, in silence, for the gap between seeing and deciding to close.

object.note: Object 5 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Something too fast to watch becomes something too fast to replay: an umpire's split-second ruling while a whole ground waits in silence.

thread_out.thread: The gap between seeing and deciding narrows further on a mountain road, where a bus driver reacts to each blind bend faster than thought, still caring for everyone on board.

requirements: An active local cricket tournament with a willing umpire and organisers
Fast, reliable camera coverage of play, including close-in shots on the umpire
Consent from players, umpires and organisers to film real matches and decisions

suggestions.name: A village or town cricket tournament
suggestions.why: Local cricket tournaments are widespread and would supply real, unstaged close decisions.
suggestions.season_notes: Cricket season and tournament calendars vary by region and school or club schedule.
suggestions.verify: A specific tournament, ground and willing umpire are unconfirmed.
